title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
oneLiner: You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems.
whatILiked: The most empowering book on human behavior I have encountered. Clear dismantles the myth that massive success requires monumental willpower. Instead, he treats identity as a daily vote: every small choice casts a ballot for who you want to become. This completely shifted how I structure my mornings and reading routines.

quotes.text: Every action you take is a vote for the type of person you wish to become. No single instance will transform your beliefs, but as the votes build up, so does the evidence of your new identity.
You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems. Your goal is your desired outcome; your system is the collection of daily habits that will get you there.
Be the designer of your world and not merely the consumer of it. Never depend on willpower when environment design can remove the friction.

stories.title: The British Cycling Renaissance
stories.summary: For nearly a century, British cyclists won almost nothing. In 2003, performance director Dave Brailsford looked for 1% improvements everywhere: redesigned bike seats for comfort, rubbed alcohol on tires for grip, and carried each rider's personal pillow to hotels for optimal sleep. Within 5 years, they dominated the Olympics and won 5 Tour de France titles.

topics.name: The 4 Laws of Behavior Change
topics.takeaway: Make it obvious (cue), Make it attractive (craving), Make it easy (response), Make it satisfying (reward). Invert these 4 to break bad habits.

topics.name: The Two-Minute Rule
topics.takeaway: When starting a new habit, scale it down until it takes less than two minutes. Standardize before you optimize.

marginalia.note: Action item: Keep my current physical book on my pillow every morning. When I head to bed, reading has zero friction!

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
oneLiner: You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
whatILiked: Reading this feels like eavesdropping on the private soul of the most powerful man in the ancient world. Marcus never intended these pages to be published; they were private self-admonitions written in military campaign tents. His humility, ruthless self-honesty, and acceptance of mortality are profoundly grounding.

quotes.text: The soul becomes dyed with the color of its thoughts. If you dwell on petty grievances, your spirit grows small. Dwell on virtue, and your mind stays expansive.
quotes.note: Curate what you allow your mind to linger on.

quotes.text: When you arise in the morning think of what a privilege it is to be alive, to think, to enjoy, to love. Meet the day not with dread, but as a temporary gift.
Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.

stories.title: Journaling Along the Frozen Danube
stories.summary: During the Marcomannic Wars, while battling brutal winter storms and a plague that ravaged Rome, Marcus sat in his military tent along the frozen Danube river. Rather than seeking revenge against political betrayals, he used his journal to remind himself to remain calm, treat difficult people with patience, and accept nature's seasons without anger.

topics.name: The Dichotomy of Control
topics.takeaway: Distinguish between things within your power (judgments, intentions, actions) and things outside it (reputation, weather, outcomes). Invest zero anxiety in the latter.

topics.name: The View from Above
topics.takeaway: Zoom out mentally until cities and disputes look like specks of dust. Cosmic scale restores harmless proportion to everyday anxieties.

marginalia.note: When someone is rude in email or traffic: Remember they act from blindness to what is truly good. They cannot stain my character unless I react in kind.

title: The Psychology of Money
author: Morgan Housel
oneLiner: Doing well with money has a little to do with how smart you are and a lot to do with how you behave.
whatILiked: Not a single boring spreadsheet or dry formula in sight. Housel treats money as a study of human psychology: ego, envy, fear, and freedom. The chapter on 'Freedom' resonated deeply — that wealth's greatest dividend is not shiny toys, but the ability to wake up every morning and control your own schedule.

quotes.text: Spending money to show people how much money you have is the fastest way to have less money. Wealth is what you don't see — the unpurchased cars, the unbought watches.
quotes.note: Wealth is financial options, not trophies.

quotes.text: The highest form of wealth is the ability to wake up every morning and say, 'I can do whatever I want today.'
Having a gap between what could happen and what you need to happen in order to do well is what gives you endurance. Room for error is the only thing that lets you survive.

stories.title: The Janitor vs The Wall Street Mogul
stories.summary: Ronald Read was a quiet gas station attendant and janitor in rural Vermont who died with over $8 million in savings, having patiently compounded blue-chip stocks for decades. In contrast, Richard Fuscone was a Harvard-educated Merrill Lynch vice chairman who borrowed heavily for an 18,000-sq-ft mansion with eleven bathrooms. In the 2008 crash, his leverage crushed him into bankruptcy.

topics.name: The Concept of 'Enough'
topics.takeaway: Modern society is engineered to move the goalposts. Financial peace begins when you recognize that risking what you need for what you don't need is madness.

topics.name: Reasonable Over Rational
topics.takeaway: Don't aim to be coldly rational on paper; aim to be emotionally reasonable so you can sleep soundly at night and stick with your plan through downturns.

marginalia.note: The real flex isn't a sportscar. It's having an unhurried, peaceful Tuesday morning sipping tea with a book, knowing your bills are covered.

title: Klara and the Sun
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
oneLiner: Do you believe in the human heart? Something that makes each of us truly special and individual?
whatILiked: Ishiguro's gentle, heartbreaking restraint. Klara, a solar-powered Artificial Friend, observes human fragility, jealousy, and unconditional love with a purity that human characters have lost. It poses lingering philosophical questions about whether human beings are truly irreplaceable.

quotes.text: The Sun always has ways to reach us. No matter how deep the shadows seem in the room, his nourishment finds a way through the glass.
There was something very special, but it wasn't inside Josie. It was inside those who loved her. You cannot copy a person without copying the love that wraps around them.

stories.title: Klara's Journey to McBain's Barn
stories.summary: Believing that the Sun rests every night inside the dark wooden beams of a distant farmer's barn, Klara sneaks across overgrown fields at twilight. She bargains with the Sun with pure devotion, offering her own solar fluid if he will only shed special nourishment to cure her ailing human companion, Josie.

topics.name: The Mystery of the Human Heart
topics.takeaway: Is a person just a complex set of habits and vocal cadences that can be replicated, or is human uniqueness held in the invisible relationships we share with others?

topics.name: Unconditional Devotion
topics.takeaway: Klara expects nothing in return for her fidelity. Her gentle acceptance of obsolescence once her duty is fulfilled is quietly devastating.

marginalia.note: Notice Ishiguro's visual framing: when Klara feels sensory or emotional overload, her field of vision breaks into compartmentalized geometric boxes.
